# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.
**Built with GitHub Actions, OpenCode, shared skills, and unreasonable optimism.** 😏

This is the OMGithub auto-build environment. The prompt.md is a sample meta prompt (FPS). User's actual request: "Make a game like GTA 5."

We need to build a browser game — a GTA-like open-world action game in Three.js presumably. Constraints: static HTML, no build needed (or vite). Since default-start supports plain index.html with no package.json, the simplest robust route: a plain static HTML + JS with Three.js from CDN? But external network at runtime may not be reliable in the preview. Better to vendor three.js locally via npm? If package.json exists, it expects vite and requires build output; that's supported. But CDN may be blocked in preview. Let's check network availability and whether three is installed/cached.

## Objective
- Build a playable GTA 5–like browser game from the user's one-line request: "Make a game that is like gta 5".

## Requirements
- User gave no further constraints; game is being built as an original stylized open-world crime sandbox (not a GTA asset/trademark clone).
- Must run as a static browser game in this environment; verified in a real browser.
- Follow implicit environment expectations: responsive desktop/mobile layout and usable touch controls.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js r160 vendored locally (`vendor/three.module.js`) with an import map and no build step.
- Original name: **Sunset City**, tagline "A neon crime sandbox".
- Scope: procedural city, third-person on-foot movement, arcade driving, traffic, pedestrians, shooting, wanted stars/police chases, 5 missions, pickups, minimap, HUD, day/night cycle, synthesized WebAudio.
- All assets/textures generated procedurally; no external models or audio files.
- Start screen must have exactly one button labeled `Play Game` so the capture harness auto-start matches.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented full project structure: `index.html`, `style.css`, 11 ES modules in `src/`.
- Procedural world: road grid, merged-texture buildings, plaza/fountain, park, casino landmark, beach/ocean shader, pier with rotating ferris wheel, neon signs, storefront windows, streetlights, rooftop props, distant hills, sky shader with sunset, stars, clouds.
- Player controller: third-person camera, WASD, sprint/jump, mouse look/aim, pistol hitscan, reload, health/armor/regen, enter/exit vehicles.
- Vehicles: procedural sedan/sports/SUV/van/taxi/police models, arcade physics, traffic AI on road grid, police pursuit, explosions/wrecks, headlights, run-overs.
- Agents: pedestrians with sidewalks/flee/corpses, foot cops and mission thugs that shoot.
- Systems: wanted stars + police spawning/decay, 5-mission chain, pickups/drops, HUD with circular minimap, objective card, wanted stars, money/clock, weapon/ammo, speedometer, toasts, mission banners, wasted/pause screens, mobile joystick/buttons.
- Fixed runtime errors encountered during browser verification (`game.scene` typo in `missions.js`, undefined `missions` shorthand in `main.js`, duplicate boot via the `#game` named-element global, missing `scene.add(player.group)`).
- Verified start screen and gameplay render; player, city, HUD, mission marker, cars now visible.

### Active
- Visual polish pass just applied but **not yet inspected**: brighter ambient/hemisphere/exposure, warmer golden-hour start time (17:35), storefront window textures, player visibility fixes. Screenshot `screenshots/game5.png` was captured after this pass and still needs review.
- Gameplay systems have not yet been interactively smoke-tested (movement, entering car, driving, shooting, wanted level, missions, mobile layout).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/game5.png`; tune lighting/contrast if still too dark or washed out (likely need to lift shadowed street/character).
2. Run browser smoke tests via `playwright-cli eval` using `window.__SUNSET` / `window.game`: move with keys, press `E` near car, drive, fire, set wanted, verify missions and HUD.
3. Verify mobile viewport rendering (390×844) and touch controls (may need `body.touch` simulation).
4. Fix known minimap water polygon (currently a rectangular fill that breaks when rotated) and add `#favicon` already handled.
5. Run `node --check src/*.js` again, then `bash capture.sh`/the capture flow if feasible; ensure no page errors beyond favicon.
6. Update `README.md` with game description and controls; remove screenshot artifacts if desired (screenshots/ is gitignored).
7. Consider committing changes (currently all work is uncommitted on `e8cddb8 Install OpenCode issue listener`).

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game orchestration, spawning, wanted system, shooting, UI binding, debug API `window.__SUNSET`.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural city/lighting/collision; current tuning hot spot.
- `src/player.js`: Player movement, camera, shooting.
- `src/vehicles.js`: Car meshes, physics, traffic/police AI.
- `src/missions.js`: Five-mission chain and marker logic.
- `src/agents.js`: Pedestrians, cops, thugs.
- `src/hud.js`: HUD/minimap updates.
- `src/effects.js`: Particle/tracer/explosion effects.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard/mouse/touch input.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized audio.
- `src/utils.js`: Texture generators incl. facades, neon, storefronts.
- `index.html`: DOM overlays and `Play Game` start button.
- `style.css`: Start screen, HUD, pause/wasted, mobile controls.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Vendored Three.js r160.

## Important Context
- Static server is running in tmux session `sunset` on `http://localhost:3002` (`PORT=3002 bash start.sh`); server log at `/tmp/opencode/server.log`.
- `playwright-cli` needed `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` earlier; browser currently open in a live session.
- Screenshot capture auto-clicks only buttons whose label exactly matches `/^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i`; keep the single `Play Game` button.
- A large dark area at the bottom of early gameplay screenshots was a building shadow, not a bug; player was missing because `Player` never added its group to the scene (now fixed).
- Debug: `window.__SUNSET.state()`, `.teleport(x,z)`, `.giveWanted(n)`, `.time(h)`, `.mission()`.
- Game starts at golden hour `world.timeOfDay = 17.35`, `dayLength = 2400`, spawn at `(0, 152)` facing north; mission marker at `(0, 118)`.
- Potential concerns to recheck: minimap `game.player.camYaw` fixed; agent hit signatures now accept `opts`; cop/police AI gated by `game.wanted`; `addCrime`/`raiseWanted` semantics.

+// Bake a solid color into a geometry so many small parts can share one
+// vertex-colored material and one draw call.
+export function paintGeometry(geo, color) {
+  const c = color instanceof THREE.Color ? color : new THREE.Color(color)
+  const count = geo.attributes.position.count
+  const arr = new Float32Array(count * 3)
+  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+    arr[i * 3] = c.r
+    arr[i * 3 + 1] = c.g
+    arr[i * 3 + 2] = c.b
+  }
+  geo.setAttribute('color', new THREE.BufferAttribute(arr, 3))
+  return geo
+}
+
+export function boxGeometry(w, h, d, color, x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, rx = 0) {
+  const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d)
+  if (rx) geo.rotateX(rx)
+  geo.translate(x, y, z)
+  return paintGeometry(geo, color)
+}
+
+// Merge geometries that all carry position/normal/uv/color attributes. Used
+// for characters and cars, where dozens of little boxes become one mesh.
+export function mergeGeometries(geos) {
+  const parts = geos.map((g) => (g.index ? g.toNonIndexed() : g))
+  const names = ['position', 'normal', 'uv', 'color'].filter((name) => parts.every((g) => g.attributes[name]))
+  let total = 0
+  for (const g of parts) total += g.attributes.position.count
+  const out = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
+  for (const name of names) {
+    const itemSize = parts[0].attributes[name].itemSize
+    const arr = new Float32Array(total * itemSize)
+    let offset = 0
+    for (const g of parts) {
+      arr.set(g.attributes[name].array, offset)
+      offset += g.attributes[name].array.length
+    }
+    out.setAttribute(name, new THREE.BufferAttribute(arr, itemSize))
+  }
+  for (const g of parts) if (!geos.includes(g)) g.dispose()
+  for (const g of geos) g.dispose()
+  out.computeBoundingSphere()
+  return out
+}

content.text:
Body computed border-radius 50% and bg rgba(10,8,16,0.46) — those are the `.touch` CSS class styles! The selector `.touch { position:absolute; pointer-events:auto; ... border-radius:50%; background: rgba(10,8,16,0.46) ... }` matches `body.touch` because we added class `touch` to body. That's the bug! The generic `.touch` class used for touch buttons also matches body. So body becomes border-radius 50% (oval) and background semi-transparent dark. That's why the 3D scene is masked by an oval and darkened. Also position absolute on body.

Fix: rename the body class from `touch` to `is-touch` or scope `.touch` selector to `#touch-buttons .touch` / `.touch` button. The simplest: change CSS `.touch {` to `#touch-buttons .touch {` and `.touch.held` to `#touch-buttons .touch.held`, `.touch.fire` etc. Also `body.touch` selectors remain valid (body class touch). But body still has class "touch" matching other CSS rules? Search `.touch` usages. Only buttons. Renaming CSS selectors should fix.

Better also rename class in JS to `mobile` to avoid collision; but index.html buttons have class "touch" and CSS. Easiest scope selectors.

However, note `.touch` class on `<button>` elements; scoping to `#touch-buttons .touch` covers all. Do it:
- `.touch {` -> `#touch-buttons .touch {`
- `.touch.held` -> `#touch-buttons .touch.held`
- `.touch.fire` -> `#touch-buttons .touch.fire`
- `.touch.aim` -> `#touch-buttons .touch.aim`
- `.touch.small` -> `#touch-buttons .touch.small`
- nth-child selectors already `#touch-buttons .touch:nth-child...` fine.

212:   drawMinimap(game) {
213:     const ctx = this.ctx
214:     const dpr = this.mapDpr || 1
215:     const size = this.mapSize || 180
216:     const r = this.mapR || 84
217:     ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0)
218:     ctx.clearRect(0, 0, size, size)
219:     const cx = size / 2
220:     const cy = size / 2
221:     const scale = 0.8
222:     const yaw = game.player.camYaw
223:     const cos = Math.cos(yaw)
224:     const sin = Math.sin(yaw)
225:     const p = game.player.car ? game.player.car.pos : game.player.pos
226:     const px = p.x
227:     const pz = p.z
228: 
229:     const toScreen = (x, z) => {
230:       const dx = x - px
231:       const dz = z - pz
232:       return [cx + (dx * cos - dz * sin) * scale, cy + (dx * sin + dz * cos) * scale]
233:     }
234: 
235:     ctx.save()
236:     ctx.beginPath()
237:     ctx.arc(cx, cy, r, 0, TAU)
238:     ctx.clip()
239:     ctx.fillStyle = '#1b2024'
240:     ctx.fillRect(0, 0, size, size)
241: 
242:     // Water / beach south
243:     const [wx, wy] = toScreen(0, 460)
244:     ctx.fillStyle = '#123a46'
245:     ctx.fillRect(0, wy, size, size)
246: 
247:     // Blocks
248:     ctx.fillStyle = '#2c3137'
249:     for (let i = -5; i < 5; i++) {
250:       for (let j = -5; j < 5; j++) {
251:         const bx = GRID * i + GRID / 2
252:         const bz = GRID * j + GRID / 2
253:         const half = 26
254:         const corners = [
255:           toScreen(bx - half, bz - half),
256:           toScreen(bx + half, bz - half),
257:           toScreen(bx + half, bz + half),
258:           toScreen(bx - half, bz + half)
259:         ]
260:         ctx.beginPath()
261:         ctx.moveTo(corners[0][0], corners[0][1])
262:         for (let k = 1; k < 4; k++) ctx.lineTo(corners[k][0], corners[k][1])
263:         ctx.closePath()
264:         ctx.fill()
265:       }
266:     }
267: 
268:     // Roads
269:     ctx.strokeStyle = '#4b5158'
270:     ctx.lineWidth = 18 * scale
271:     for (let line = -5; line <= 5; line++) {
272:       const p0 = toScreen(GRID * line, -CITY_EDGE)
273:       const p1 = toScreen(GRID * line, CITY_EDGE)
274:       ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(p0[0], p0[1]); ctx.lineTo(p1[0], p1[1]); ctx.stroke()
275:       const p2 = toScreen(-CITY_EDGE, GRID * line)
276:       const p3 = toScreen(CITY_EDGE, GRID * line)
277:       ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(p2[0], p2[1]); ctx.lineTo(p3[0], p3[1]); ctx.stroke()
278:     }
279: 
280:     // Mission marker
281:     const missionPos = game.missions.getMarkerPos()
282:     if (missionPos) {
283:       const [mx, my] = toScreen(missionPos.x, missionPos.z)
284:       ctx.save()
285:       ctx.translate(mx, my)
286:       ctx.rotate(Math.PI / 4)
287:       ctx.fillStyle = '#ffd24a'
288:       ctx.strokeStyle = '#5a4300'
289:       ctx.lineWidth = 1.5
290:       ctx.fillRect(-5, -5, 10, 10)
291:       ctx.strokeRect(-5, -5, 10, 10)
292:       ctx.restore()
293:     }
294: 
295:     // Pickups
296:     for (const pickup of game.pickups) {
297:       if (pickup.taken) continue
298:       const [ix, iy] = toScreen(pickup.pos.x, pickup.pos.z)
299:       if ((ix - cx) ** 2 + (iy - cy) ** 2 > r * r) continue
300:       ctx.fillStyle = pickup.type === 'health' ? '#6dff8a' : pickup.type === 'armor' ? '#6db7ff' : '#ffd24a'
301:       ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ix, iy, 2.2, 0, TAU); ctx.fill()
302:     }
303: 
304:     // Traffic
305:     for (const v of game.vehicles) {
306:       if (v.occupiedByPlayer || v.destroyed) continue
307:       const [vx, vy] = toScreen(v.pos.x, v.pos.z)
308:       if ((vx - cx) ** 2 + (vy - cy) ** 2 > r * r) continue
309:       ctx.fillStyle = v.police ? '#7fa8ff' : '#d7d7d7'
310:       ctx.fillRect(vx - 1.5, vy - 1.5, 3, 3)
311:     }
312: 
313:     // Cops
314:     for (const cop of game.cops) {
315:       if (cop.dead) continue
316:       const [ox, oy] = toScreen(cop.pos.x, cop.pos.z)
317:       if ((ox - cx) ** 2 + (oy - cy) ** 2 > r * r) continue
318:       ctx.fillStyle = '#ff5050'
319:       ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox, oy, 2.6, 0, TAU); ctx.fill()
320:     }
321:     for (const v of game.vehicles) {
322:       if (!v.police || v.destroyed) continue
323:       const [ox, oy] = toScreen(v.pos.x, v.pos.z)
324:       if ((ox - cx) ** 2 + (oy - cy) ** 2 > r * r) continue
325:       ctx.fillStyle = Math.sin(performance.now() * 0.012) > 0 ? '#ff3030' : '#3060ff'
326:       ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox, oy, 3.4, 0, TAU); ctx.fill()
327:     }
328: 
329:     // Player arrow
330:     ctx.save()
331:     ctx.translate(cx, cy)
332:     ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff'
333:     ctx.strokeStyle = '#12151a'
334:     ctx.lineWidth = 1.4
335:     ctx.beginPath()
336:     ctx.moveTo(0, -8)
337:     ctx.lineTo(5.5, 6)
338:     ctx.lineTo(0, 3)
339:     ctx.lineTo(-5.5, 6)
340:     ctx.closePath()
341:     ctx.fill()
342:     ctx.stroke()
343:     ctx.restore()
344: 
345:     // North marker
346:     ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.55)'
347:     ctx.font = 'bold 9px Arial'
348:     ctx.textAlign = 'center'
349:     const nx = cx + Math.sin(yaw) * (r - 10)
350:     const ny = cy - Math.cos(yaw) * (r - 10)
351:     ctx.fillText('N', nx, ny + 3)
352: 
353:     ctx.restore()
354: 
355:     // Border
356:     ctx.beginPath()
357:     ctx.arc(cx, cy, r, 0, TAU)
358:     ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.28)'
359:     ctx.lineWidth = 2
360:     ctx.stroke()
361:     ctx.beginPath()
362:     ctx.arc(cx, cy, r + 1.5, 0, TAU)
363:     ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.55)'
364:     ctx.lineWidth = 2
365:     ctx.stroke()
366:   }
367: }

369: function locName(pos) {
370:   const beach = pos.z > 340
371:   if (beach) return 'Vice Beach'
372:   const x = pos.x

374:   if (Math.abs(x) < 90 && Math.abs(z) < 90) return 'Downtown'
375:   if (x < -80 && z > 80) return 'West Grove'
376:   if (x > 120 && z < -40) return 'Casino Strip'
377:   if (z < -150) return 'Northside'
378:   if (x > 150) return 'East Docks'
379:   return 'Sunset City'
380: }

Minimap water: `ctx.fillRect(0, wy, size, size)` ignores rotation. When yaw=0 and looking north, water is south, wy should be > center, but minimap is north-up-ish? Actually toScreen rotates map with yaw; water boundary should be a rotated line, not horizontal. We can fix by drawing a rotated rectangle or polygon. Since the minimap rotates with camera yaw, draw the water as a polygon covering the region z > 450. Compute four corners of a large region: x from -1000 to 1000, z from 450 to 1000, project each to screen, fill polygon. Use toScreen on (-1000,450),(1000,450),(1000,1200),(-1000,1200). Clip already. That handles rotation.

Do that.

Also improve minimap "N" marker visibility and player arrow rotation? Player arrow always points up while map rotates with camYaw. That's standard (north-up? Actually map rotates, arrow should point toward player heading relative to camera). Player arrow currently fixed up, so map orientation is camera-relative; arrow fixed up is okay-ish, but should indicate player facing: arrow could rotate by heading-camYaw. The map is camera-relative so forward relative to camera rotates. Fine; not necessary.

Now fix pause position, minimap water polygon, and plaza sign rotation. Also maybe remove brand banner lasting into gameplay? It's a 3.6s intro banner, acceptable. But screenshots at start show SUNSET CITY across center, covering action. The capture harness likely takes screenshot shortly after clicking, so the giant title in the middle may hurt first impression. It lasts 3.6 game seconds (with real dt), but at 2fps dt cap 0.05 means bannerTimer decreases by 0.05 per frame; at 2.7fps that's 0.135/sec → takes 26 real seconds to fade! That's why screenshots after 2s/3s still show it. On a real 60fps browser it fades in 3.6s. But in the harness low FPS, it lingers a long time. Also the initial "SUNSET CITY" banner blocks the view. We should shorten or avoid the banner when the start screen already shows the logo. Better: don't show the big "SUNSET CITY" banner on startGame; instead toast "WELCOME TO SUNSET" or show a compact objective update. The logo already appeared on start screen. Removing the center banner improves gameplay screenshots and avoids the banner lingering. We can keep mission start banners (those are contextual). In startGame, replace `this.hud.banner('SUNSET CITY', 'A neon crime sandbox', 3.6)` with maybe no banner or a short 1.2s "SUNSET CITY" if desired. I'd remove it entirely; the HUD is enough. Maybe toast "WELCOME TO SUNSET CITY" appears (toast at top). That wouldn't block center. Let's change to `this.hud.toast('WELCOME TO SUNSET CITY', 'gold')` after a short timeout or immediately.

Also the "MISSION PASSED" banner stuck in mobile screenshot due to low FPS and dt cap. It will fade eventually but in screenshots after mission tests it's there. On real 60fps, 4s. Fine. For capture at boot, no banner.

Also the HUD toast at top center overlaps objective on mobile; that's okay.
